elements.element: Renewal must be structured either as renewal only by mutual written agreement or as automatic renewal.
elements.evidence: The clause uses automatic renewal: “will automatically renew.”

elements.element: If automatic renewal is used, each renewal term must be 12 months.
If automatic renewal is used, Customer must be able to opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Automatic renewal is used, but Customer must give at least 60 days' prior written notice, rather than 30 days' notice.

elements.element: If automatic renewal is used, Vendor must provide Customer a renewal reminder 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: Automatic renewal is used, but the operative language contains no Vendor reminder obligation.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase must be capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.
elements.evidence: The operative language contains no cap on renewal price increases. The margin comment cannot supply the omitted restriction.
The clause states that the Agreement “will automatically renew.”

elements.element: The required non-renewal notice period must be no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Customer may prevent renewal by giving at least 60 days' prior written notice, making 60 days the required advance-notice deadline.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase must not exceed 5%.
elements.evidence: No operative language limits renewal price increases to 5% or less.

result.reason: The redline adds a relevant Customer non-renewal right and preserves the existing termination and breach provisions without contradiction. It meets the fallback notice period but omits the fallback 5% price cap, so it reaches neither a complete preferred nor fallback position. The retained 90-day post-Initial-Term termination right overlaps with, but does not negate, the new non-renewal mechanism.
